transcript.answer: At most three upkeep runs can start per repository for each event, such as a push to main. The pull requests that go first are the ones upkept longest ago. Order: a pull request never upkept comes first. Next is the one whose newest upkeep run started earliest. Last is the oldest pull request. This rule was added on 2026-10-25 (FR12.19a). Before it, the three oldest pull requests always got the starts. When those three kept failing, they starved every other loop pull request. Examples are re-cinq/lore #2879, #2880 and #2881. The rest wait for the next event. Upkeep also only applies to loop pull requests that GitHub reports as behind main under a branch rule. Pull requests whose ticket is parked with `lore:blocked` are skipped.
